questions.prompt: Differentiate \(f(z)=z^3+2e^z\).
questions.answer: Both parts are analytic functions of \(z\). Differentiate term by term: \[f'(z)=3z^2+2e^z\]

questions.prompt: Does \(f(z)=z+\overline z\) have a complex derivative?
questions.answer: Since \(z+\overline z=2x\), the function depends on direction in the plane. The conjugate term is not complex differentiable, and the Cauchy-Riemann equations fail except not enough to produce a neighbourhood of analyticity. Treat it as non-analytic.
